Subject: [Action Required] Enable 2-step verification to maintain your access to the Google Cloud console

2SV will be required for Google Cloud console access starting Oct 20, 2026.




MY CONSOLE




Hello Tech,

We're writing to inform you about an upcoming security update for your  
organization.

Starting October 20, 2026, you will be required to use 2-Step Verification  
(2SV) to access the Google Cloud console.

We have provided additional information below to guide you through this  
change.

What you need to know

In November 2024, we first announced that Google Cloud would be doing a  
phased roll out of mandatory 2SV, also known as multi-factor authentication  
(MFA). Two-step verification adds an additional layer of security by  
requiring users to provide both a password and a second verification  
method—such as a security key, a phone-based prompt, or a Google  
Authenticator code—during sign in.

Key changes:

Starting October 20, 2026, you must use 2SV to access the Google Cloud  
console and Firebase console with your Google Cloud Identity account.

Your administrator can extend this deadline by 90 days. Watch for updates  
from your IT department about the final date when your organization will  
enforce 2SV.

What you need to do

Action advised: If you're using Google Cloud organization 1072058966898,  
you must turn on 2-Step Verification for your account at  
security.google.com by October 20, 2026.

If you cannot see the 2SV option, contact your administrator for assistance.

What is not affected:


Apps and workloads that run on Google Cloud, including those using Google  
APIs
Google Workspace products, such as Gmail, Google Sheets, and Google Slides.  
These have their own 2SV requirement programs. Review the 2SV requirements  
for the Google products you use.

We're here to help

We understand that this change may require some planning, and we're here to  
support you during this process. For more information, refer to the  
multi-factor authentication requirement documentation. If you have  
questions or need assistance, contact your administrator.

Thanks for choosing Google Cloud.





– The Google Cloud Team

apps you use. We've updated our Privacy Policy to be clearer about the data we 
collect and how we use it. We encourage you to read the updated Privacy Policy 
in full, but we’ve set out a summary of the key changes below:

tasks and works with third-party apps and services, we've explained the data 
this involves — including how data can flow to and from third parties when you 
connect a service or have Claude do tasks on your behalf.


2. Verification data. As part of our measures to keep our services safe and 
secure we may ask you to verify your age or identity, and we've described what 
we collect and how.


3. Study participation. If you take part in Anthropic studies, surveys, or 
interviews, we've explained the information we collect.


4. Additional information about our data practices. We’ve provided more detail 
about how we communicate with you and promote our services, including providing 
tailored recommendations about our services that may be of interest to you. 
We've also clarified the circumstances under which we may receive or provide 
data to third parties, and the legal bases we rely on when processing your data.


 While our products have evolved, our commitments haven't: We don’t sell your 
data, Claude remains ad-free, and you can control whether your chats and coding 
sessions are used to train and improve Anthropic’s AI models.


Learn more

Hi Tech, we've refined how access works in Attio.

Permissions are returning to additive only, so the most permissive grant always wins, whether it's set at the workspace, team, or individual level.

Start with safe defaults at the workspace level, then grant more access to specific teams or people as needed. Each level can only grant more access, not less.

Nothing you've already set up needs to change. All your existing permissions will continue to work as expected.

This change was made to simplify permissions for workflows.

Workflows now inherit the workspace
default again, making them easier to build as members and agents increasingly work side by side.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html dir="ltr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta http-equiv="x-ua-compatible" content="ie=edge">
  <title></title>
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <!-- Hint clients that we explicitly support light/dark rendering. -->
  <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark only">
  <meta name="supported-color-schemes" content="light dark only">
  
  <style type="text/css">
    @media screen and (max-width:480px) {
      .text-only-email-title-with-break {
        font-size:30px !important;
        line-height:36px !important;
      }
    }
  </style>

  <style type="text/css">
  /**
   * Google webfonts. Recommended to include the .woff version for cross-client compatibility.
   */
  @media screen {
    /* OpenAI Sans font family */
    @font-face {
      font-display: swap;
      font-family: "OpenAI Sans";
      font-style: normal;
      font-weight: 400;
      src: url("https://cdn.openai.com/common/fonts/openai-sans/v2/OpenAISans-Regular.woff2") format("woff2");
    }

    @font-face {
      font-display: swap;
      font-family: "OpenAI Sans";
      font-style: normal;
      font-weight: 500;
      src: url("https://cdn.openai.com/common/fonts/openai-sans/v2/OpenAISans-Medium.woff2") format("woff2");
    }

    @font-face {
      font-display: swap;
      font-family: "OpenAI Sans";
      font-style: normal;
      font-weight: 600;
      src: url("https://cdn.openai.com/common/fonts/openai-sans/v2/OpenAISans-Semibold.woff2") format("woff2");
    }

    @font-face {
      font-display: swap;
      font-family: "OpenAI Sans";
      font-style: normal;
      font-weight: 700;
      src: url("https://cdn.openai.com/common/fonts/openai-sans/v2/OpenAISans-Bold.woff2") format("woff2");
    }
  }

  :root {
    color-scheme: light dark only;
    supported-color-schemes: light dark only;
  }

  /**
   * Avoid browser level font resizing.
   * 1. Windows Mobile
   * 2. iOS / OSX
   */
  body,
  table,
  td,
  a {
    -ms-text-size-adjust: 100%; /* 1 */
    -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; /* 2 */
    font-family: 'OpenAI Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
  }

  /**
   * Remove extra space added to tables and cells in Outlook.
   */
  table,
  td {
    mso-table-rspace: 0pt;
    mso-table-lspace: 0pt;
    vertical-align: top; /* Align content to the top of table cells */
  }

  /**
   * Better fluid images in Internet Explorer.
   */
  img {
    -ms-interpolation-mode: bicubic;
  }

  /**
   * Remove blue links for iOS devices.
   */
  a[x-apple-data-detectors] {
    font-family: inherit !important;
    font-size: inherit !important;
    font-weight: inherit !important;
    line-height: inherit !important;
    color: inherit !important;
    text-decoration: none !important;
  }

  /**
   * Fix centering issues in Android 4.4.
   */
  div[style*="margin: 16px 0;"] {
    margin: 0 !important;
  }

  body {
    width: 100% !important;
    height: 100% !important;
    padding: 0 !important;
    margin: 0 !important;
  }

  /**
   * Collapse table borders to avoid space between cells.
   */
  table {
    border-collapse: collapse !important;
  }

  a {
    color: #898A8D;
  }

  .image-reset-bullets,
  .image-reset-bullets .email-bullet-link {
      color: #000000;
  }

  /* Give the ChatGPT logo pill consistent breathing room in light mode. */
  .email-logo-pill {
      background-color: #ffffff;
      border-radius: 12px;
      padding: 13px;
      display: inline-block;
  }

  img {
    height: auto;
    line-height: 100%;
    text-decoration: none;
    border: 0;
    outline: none;
  }

  /* Composer image sizing (mobile default) */
  .composer-img {
      width: 83px !important;
      height: auto !important;
      padding: 16px !important;
  }

  h1 {
      font-size: 34px;
      line-height: 41px;
      font-weight: 400;
      letter-spacing: 0.4px;
      margin: 0;
  }
  h2 {
      font-size: 18px;
      font-weight: 400;
      margin: 0;
      line-height: 150%;
      letter-spacing: -0.2px;
  }
  p {
      font-size: 16px;
      line-height: 130%;
      font-weight: 500;
      margin: 0;
  }
  p + p {
      margin-top: 16px;
  }
  /* Intro blocks (H1/H2) sizing */
  .intro-block {
      width: 345px !important;
      max-width: 345px !important;
  }
  /* Composer card sizing */
  .composer-card {
      width: 377px !important;
      max-width: 377px !important;
  }
  /* Button styling */
  a.button {
      background-color: #000000 !important; /* default black */
      border-radius: 24px !important; /* make button curvy */
      padding: 11.5px 24px 11.5px !important; /* bigger size */
      font-size: 16px !important; /* revert text size */
      line-height: 24px !important;
  }

  a.button:active {
      background-color: #414141 !important; /* dark gray on click */
      border-radius: 36px !important;
  }
  /* CTA button hover state (supported clients only) */
  a.button-invert:hover,
  a.button-invert:focus {
      background-color: #000000 !important;
      background-image: none !important;
      color: #FFFFFF !important;
      border-color: #FFFFFF !important;
  }
  a.button-invert:hover span,
  a.button-invert:focus span {
      color: #FFFFFF !important;
  }
  @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
      a.button-invert {
          background-color: #FFFFFF !important;
          background-image: linear-gradient(#FFFFFF, #FFFFFF) !important;
          color: #000000 !important;
          border-color: #FFFFFF !important;
          -webkit-text-fill-color: #000000 !important;
      }
      a.button-invert span {
          color: #000000 !important;
          -webkit-text-fill-color: #000000 !important;
      }
  }
  [data-ogsc] a.button-invert,
  [data-ogsb] a.button-invert {
      background-color: #FFFFFF !important;
      background-image: linear-gradient(#FFFFFF, #FFFFFF) !important;
      color: #000000 !important;
      border-color: #FFFFFF !important;
      -webkit-text-fill-color: #000000 !important;
  }
  [data-ogsc] a.button-invert span,
  [data-ogsb] a.button-invert span {
      color: #000000 !important;
      -webkit-text-fill-color: #000000 !important;
  }
  /* Ensure hover keeps text legible even with dark-mode overrides. */
  a.button-invert:hover,
  a.button-invert:focus {
      color: #FFFFFF !important;
      -webkit-text-fill-color: #FFFFFF !important;
  }
  a.button-invert:hover span,
  a.button-invert:focus span {
      color: #FFFFFF !important;
      -webkit-text-fill-color: #FFFFFF !important;
  }
  /* Badges: use real rows so the stacked layout survives across email clients */
  .badges {
      width: 100% !important;
      max-width: 128px !important;
  }
  .badges .badge {
      width: 100% !important;
      vertical-align: bottom !important;
  }
  .badges .badge img {
      width: 120px !important;
      max-width: 120px !important;
      height: auto !important;
      margin: 0 auto !important;
  }

  /* Desktop: larger typography */
  @media screen and (min-width:480px) {
      h1 {
          font-size: 34px !important;
          line-height: 41px !important;
          letter-spacing: 0.4px;
          font-weight: 400 !important;
      }
      h2 {
        font-size: 18px;
        font-weight: 400;
        margin: 0;
        line-height: 150%;
        letter-spacing: -0.2px;
      }
      /* Header cell: increase side padding on desktop only */
      td.header-td {
          padding-left: 57px !important;
          padding-right: 57px !important;
      }
      /* Composer image sizing for desktop */
      .composer-img {
          width: 98px !important;
      }
      /* Body content cells: increase side padding on desktop */
      td.content-td {
          padding-left: 60px !important;
          padding-right: 60px !important;
      }
      td.footer-td {
          padding-left: 56px !important;
          padding-right: 56px !important;
      }
      p {
          font-size: 16px !important;
          line-height: 130% !important;
          font-weight: 400;
      }
      td {
          font-size: 10px !important;
          line-height: 16px !important;
          font-weight: 400;
      }
      a.button {
          font-size: 16px !important;
          line-height: 24px !important;
      }
      .footer-row td {
          vertical-align: bottom !important;
          padding-left: 0 !important;
      }
      /* Composer card width on desktop */
      .composer-card {
          width: 400px !important;
          max-width: 400px !important;
      }
      /* Intro blocks width on desktop */
      .intro-block {
          width: 360px !important;
          max-width: 360px !important;
      }
  }
  /* Mobile stacking helper for columns */
  @media screen and (max-width:480px) {
      /* Ensure footer badges bottom-align with copyright on mobile */
      td.header-td {
          padding-left: 21px !important;
          padding-right: 21px !important;
      }
      /* Body content cells: smaller side padding on mobile */
      td.content-td {
          padding-left: 24px !important;
          padding-right: 24px !important;
      }
      td.footer-td {
          padding-left: 20px !important;
          padding-right: 20px !important;
      }
      .footer-row td {
          vertical-align: bottom !important;
          padding-left: 0 !important;
      }
  }

  /* Dark mode: render the email on a true-black canvas with high-contrast cards */

      body.generic,
      .wrapperMod,
      .heroMod03 {
          background-color: #000000 !important;
      }
      body {
          background-color: #000000 !important;
          color: #ffffff !important;
      }
      .email-shell {
          background-color: #000000 !important;
      }
      .content-td {
          background-color: #000000 !important;
      }
      h1, h2, p {
          color: #ffffff !important;
      }
      .heroMod03 h1,
      .heroMod03 h2,
      .heroMod03 p,
      .box h1,
      .box h2,
      .box p,
      .box a {
          color: #FFFFFF !important;
          -webkit-text-fill-color: #FFFFFF !important;
      }
      .prompt-card-table {
          background: #000000 !important;
          box-shadow: none !important;
      }
      .prompt-card-border {
          border-color: #FFFFFF !important;
      }
      .prompt-card-text,
      .prompt-card-text h2 {
          color: #FFFFFF !important;
      }
      .email-header-td {
          background-color: #000000 !important;
          padding-top: 8px !important;
          padding-bottom: 8px !important;
      }
      .email-header-inner {
          padding-top: 16px !important;
          padding-bottom: 16px !important;
      }
      .email-footer-surface {
          background-color: #1f1f1f !important;
          border-radius: 16px !important;
          padding: 24px !important;
      }
      .email-footer-row {
          background-color: #000000 !important;
      }

          padding-bottom: 12px !important;

          border-radius: 16px !important;

      }
      .email-logo-pill img {

      }
      .email-footer-logo-img {
          width: 90px !important;
          height: auto !important;
      }
      .email-footer-copy {
          color: #ffffff !important;
          padding-left: 0 !important;
      }
      .email-footer-copy a {
          color: #ffffff !important;

AI-MALL and WhatsApp Automation Workﬂow Prepared: 9 September 2026 Website: aimall24.com Related WhatsApp automation product: AISA Connect Author: Manus AI 1. Executive Summary AI-MALL is an AI application and intelligent-agent marketplace. Its public homepage describes it as “India’s First AI App Marketplace” and presents a concept in which users discover, integrate, deploy, and scale AI tools and agents. The website exposes user journeys such as “Marketplace,” “My Agents,” and “Become a Vendor.” AI-MALL is therefore not simply a chatbot website. Its intended model is a platform where diﬀerent vendors list AI applications or agents and customers discover and use solutions according to their business requirements. The most important ﬁnding for our WhatsApp workﬂow is that the public AI-MALL website does not expose a clear public API reference, webhook documentation, complete app catalog, pricing catalog, or developer integration guide. The frontend bundle contains indications of agent, marketplace, vendor registration, vendor chat, contact-vendor, and buy-agent routes, but their production request and response contracts are not publicly documented. Direct backend integration with AI-MALL should therefore currently be treated as an unveriﬁed integration. The public AISA Connect page, separately operated under the UWO ecosystem, claims to provide oﬃcial Meta WhatsApp API access, AI replies, lead capture, follow-ups, workﬂow building, CRM synchronization, analytics, and broadcasts. The practical initial approach should therefore be to run WhatsApp conversations and automation through AISA Connect or the Meta WhatsApp Cloud API, while using AI-MALL as the discovery, recommendation, vendor-contact, or downstream solution layer. Direct AI-MALL API integration should be added only after the AI-MALL team provides written details about its API, authentication, webhooks, and agent execution model. 2. What Is AI-MALL? AI-MALL is a vendor marketplace for intelligent agents. A marketplace allows diﬀerent solution providers to make AI products or agents available on one platform. A customer can search for a tool, understand its intended use, and contact the relevant vendor. The public homepage describes the following four-step ﬂow: The homepage footer presents AI-MALL as an “India’s First AI App Marketplace” platform with “100 AI Apps” and “Partner Integrations,” powered by UWO. These ﬁgures and positioning statements are public website claims and should be re-veriﬁed through a live catalog or oﬃcial commercial material before implementation. 3. What Can Be Done with AI-MALL? Based on the public information, the platform is intended to support the following activities: Stage Website meaning Business meaning Browse Find tools and resourcesDiscover an AI app or agent for a speciﬁc requirement IntegrateConnect through seamless integrationConnect the selected solution to a business process Deploy Start or use resourcesPut the agent or application into operation ScaleExpand workﬂows and automationHandle more users, processes, or business volume Activity User beneﬁt AI solution discoveryFind suitable agents for writing, monitoring, sales, support, operations, or other business needs Agent comparisonCompare vendors or solutions by business problem and capability Vendor contactAsk a vendor questions or share a requirement Agent purchase or useWhere available, purchase, activate, or add an agent to an account My Agents managementView agents purchased, selected, or created by the user Vendor onboardingRegister an AI application for marketplace listing Frontend route evidence includes paths such as /agents, /agents/marketplace, /agents/created-by-me, /agents/buy, /vendor/register, /vendor-chat, /messages/contact-vendor, and vendor approval routes. This suggests that the internal product model is designed for user accounts, vendor onboarding, agent submission, purchases, and vendor communication rather than only static listings. The complete operational behavior of these ﬂows could not be veriﬁed through public access. 4. Who Is AI-MALL For? 4.1 Business users Business owners and teams can use an AI marketplace to ﬁnd agents for customer support, lead qualiﬁcation, sales, reporting, monitoring, content, operations, and internal productivity. 4.2 Startups and SMEs Small and medium-sized businesses may select ready-made solutions instead of building every AI capability from scratch. This can reduce initial development time, but vendor quality, data handling, pricing, and support must be evaluated separately. 4.3 Enterprises For enterprises, the possible value lies in partner integrations, scalable workﬂows, and orchestration of multiple agents. Before enterprise adoption, request a security review, data-residency information, service-level agreement, audit logs, access controls, incident response process, and contract terms. 4.4 AI vendors and freelancers The vendor registration page asks for vendor name, email address, company name, company type, and password. The visible company-type options include Startup, SME, Enterprise, and Individual/Freelancer. The intended process is for vendor submissions to be reviewed and then listed or sold on the marketplace. 5. WhatsApp Policy and Messaging Constraints Meta states that webhook endpoints receive incoming messages and outgoing status events. Production setup requires webhook veriﬁcation, the appropriate permissions, and subscribed webhook ﬁelds. Meta can retry failed webhook deliveries, so duplicate events must be prevented through idempotent processing using the event or message ID.1 Meta documentation states that a customer service window opens after a user replies. Non- template messages can be sent during this window. Outside the window, business-initiated messages require approved message templates. Templates have a category, language, and deﬁned components, and they must pass review before they can be sent.2 3 The workﬂow should therefore include the following safeguards: •Record consent and opt-out status for outbound campaigns. •Keep marketing, utility, and authentication templates separate. •Never send an unapproved template in production. •Store the timestamp of the customer’s latest inbound message. •Use an approved template outside the 24-hour customer service window. •Do not collect unnecessary sensitive data in WhatsApp chats. •Apply role-based access to transcripts during human handoﬀ. •Obtain consent before sharing user data with a vendor. 10. AI-MALL is an AI application and intelligent-agent marketplace. Its public homepage 
describes it as “India’s First AI App Marketplace” and presents a concept in which users 
discover, integrate, deploy, and scale AI tools and agents. The website exposes user 
journeys such as “Marketplace,” “My Agents,” and “Become a Vendor.”

diﬀerent vendors list AI applications or agents and customers discover and use solutions 
according to their business requirements.
The most important ﬁnding for our WhatsApp workﬂow is that the public AI-MALL website 
does not expose a clear public API reference, webhook documentation, complete app 
catalog, pricing catalog, or developer integration guide. The frontend bundle contains 
indications of agent, marketplace, vendor registration, vendor chat, contact-vendor, and 
buy-agent routes, but their production request and response contracts are not publicly 
documented. Direct backend integration with AI-MALL should therefore currently be

The public AISA Connect page, separately operated under the UWO ecosystem, claims to

vendor-contact, or downstream solution layer. Direct AI-MALL API integration should be 
added only after the AI-MALL team provides written details about its API, authentication, 
webhooks, and agent execution model.

For the ﬁrst version, static catalog plus vendor referral is preferable because it avoids 
unsupported API assumptions.
7. Proposed WhatsApp Conversation Workﬂow
7.1 Entry points
Users may begin a WhatsApp conversation through:
•A “Chat on WhatsApp” button on the website.
•A Meta Click-to-WhatsApp advertisement.
•A QR code or business proﬁle link.
•A direct message from an existing customer.
•A vendor or partner referral.

7.5 Lead scoring
The initial lead score can use this logic:
•High intent: The user has shared the business problem, budget, and timeline.
•Medium intent: The user wants to understand the solution but has not speciﬁed 
budget or timeline.
•Low intent: The user is only browsing or requesting general information.
•Vendor lead: The user wants to list an AI application.
High-intent leads should be sent immediately to a human sales representative or relevant 
vendor. Low-intent users should receive educational content, catalog links, and a demo 
option.
7.6 Follow-up workﬂow
Follow-ups must be sent only with appropriate consent and in accordance with WhatsApp 
policies. Provide a clear STOP or UNSUBSCRIBE option.

According to Meta’s oﬃcial documentation, WhatsApp Cloud API supports sending 
messages and receiving webhooks. Incoming messages and outgoing message-status 
updates are delivered through webhooks. A production implementation requires a public 
HTTPS webhook endpoint, veriﬁcation, idempotent processing, and retry handling.1 2

status, supported language, and last veriﬁed date.
5.Automation engine: Manage rules, menus, reminders, routing, and templates.
6.AI layer: Perform intent extraction, FAQ answering, and requirement summarisation.
7.CRM integration: Store qualiﬁed leads, ownership, and status.
8.Admin dashboard: Display conversations, leads, catalog entries, and workﬂow 
performance.
9.Human inbox: Respond to escalated conversations.
9. WhatsApp Policy and Messaging Constraints
Meta states that webhook endpoints receive incoming messages and outgoing status 
events. Production setup requires webhook veriﬁcation, the appropriate permissions, and 
subscribed webhook ﬁelds. Meta can retry failed webhook deliveries, so duplicate events 
must be prevented through idempotent processing using the event or message ID.1
Meta documentation states that a customer service window opens after a user replies. Non-
template messages can be sent during this window. Outside the window, business-initiated 
messages require approved message templates. Templates have a category, language, and 
deﬁned components, and they must pass review before they can be sent.2 3
The workﬂow should therefore include the following safeguards:
•Record consent and opt-out status for outbound campaigns.
•Keep marketing, utility, and authentication templates separate.
•Never send an unapproved template in production.
•Store the timestamp of the customer’s latest inbound message.
•Use an approved template outside the 24-hour customer service window.
•Do not collect unnecessary sensitive data in WhatsApp chats.
•Apply role-based access to transcripts during human handoﬀ.
•Obtain consent before sharing user data with a vendor.
10. Questions to Conﬁrm with AI-MALL/UWO
Before starting direct integration, request written answers to the following questions:
1.Does AI-MALL provide a public or partner API?
2.What are the API base URL, version, and OpenAPI/Swagger speciﬁcation?
3.What authentication method is used: API key, OAuth, JWT, or partner token?
4.Which endpoints support agent listing, search, details, purchase, and execution?
5.Are inbound and outbound webhooks available?
6.How are webhook signatures veriﬁed and retries handled?
7.Is vendor contact or vendor chat API access available to external partners?
8.Are pricing and availability available through a real-time API or managed manually?
9.Does agent execution or customer conversation data reach AI-MALL servers?
10.What are the data-retention, deletion, encryption, and access-control policies?
11.Is an oﬃcial AISA Connect API, SDK, or partner integration available for WhatsApp 
automation?
12.What is the process for onboarding an existing WhatsApp number?
13.Who manages Meta Business veriﬁcation and billing?
14.What are the support SLA, escalation process, and outage communication procedures?
15.What are the commission, attribution, and ownership rules for vendor referrals?

MVP. Then stabilise production messaging through AISA Connect or Meta Cloud API. Keep 
direct AI-MALL API integration as a third phase.
12. MVP Scope
The ﬁrst release should include only the following:
•Hindi and English welcome ﬂows.
•Five to eight primary categories.
•Requirement collection through WhatsApp buttons or list messages.
•A curated AI-MALL catalog.
•Up to three recommended solutions per lead.
•Vendor contact request.
•Human handoﬀ.
•Consent and opt-out tracking.
•Basic lead dashboard.
•Approved follow-up templates.
•Delivery, read, and failure logging.
The ﬁrst version should not include arbitrary agent execution, payment collection, sensitive 
document processing, or fully autonomous commercial commitments.

period

roles

letter queue, and alerting

sharing consent, and preference history

processing_status.
15. KPIs
Track the following metrics after launch:
•First response time.
•Message delivery and read rate.
•Requirement-completion rate.
•Qualiﬁed-lead rate.
•Recommendation click rate.
•Vendor-contact request rate.
•Human-handoﬀ rate.
•Demo-booking rate.
•Follow-up reply rate.
•Opt-out and block rate.
•AI fallback rate.
•Lead-to-sale conversion.
•Cost per qualiﬁed lead.
Correct routing, useful recommendations, and qualiﬁed conversion are more important 
than reply speed alone. Vendor marketing claims such as “0.1 second” or “0.3 second” 
should not be treated as internal SLA commitments. Measure actual production latency 
through monitoring.
16. Additional Technical Veriﬁcation Findings
The public robots.txt points to AI-MALL’s sitemap.xml. The sitemap lists the homepage and 
routes such as /dashboard/marketplace, /login, /signup, /series, /vendor-register, /vendor-
login, /dashboard/security, /blog, and /about. This conﬁrms that the platform includes or 
plans authenticated marketplace, vendor onboarding, and security-related product areas. 
The presence of a route in the sitemap does not prove that the complete content is 
available without login.
The frontend bundle contains logic to read the backend URL from runtime environment 
variables: VITE_AIMALL_BACKEND_API, VITE_BACKEND_API, or VITE_API_URL. No production 
backend hostname, OpenAPI speciﬁcation, Swagger page, or public webhook contract was 
found in the public HTML or inspected conﬁguration. Therefore, the external WhatsApp 
workﬂow should not depend directly on internal endpoints merely because route names 
are visible. Direct API integration remains unveriﬁed until oﬃcial access and 
documentation are provided.
Bundle inspection also veriﬁed names of internal service routes, including /agents, 
/agents/marketplace, /agents/{id}/details, /agents/buy/{id}, /agents/get_my_agents, /chat, 
/vendor-chat, /vendor-chat/message, /messages/contact-vendor, /support, and vendor 
approval/submission routes. These names indicate possible integration surfaces, but the 
request schemas, response schemas, permissions, rate limits, billing behavior, and stability 
have not been veriﬁed through public documentation. Oﬃcial partner credentials and an 
API contract are required before depending directly on these routes.
The frontend JavaScript also contains a client-side application identiﬁer and application 
key associated with the aimall application. Any key available in a browser must not be 
treated as a conﬁdential secret. If the key grants privileged access, it should be scope-
restricted, rotated, and protected through server-side authorisation. WhatsApp access 
tokens, vendor credentials, payment credentials, and user-data tokens must never be 
embedded in a frontend bundle.
17. Final Conclusion
AI-MALL should be understood as an AI solutions marketplace and agent ecosystem. 
Users can discover AI tools, vendors can submit applications, and businesses can search for 
solutions to speciﬁc workﬂow problems.
The public AI-MALL website alone does not provide enough technical documentation for a 
WhatsApp workﬂow. Do not treat it as the WhatsApp backend. Use Meta Cloud API or AISA 
Connect as the messaging and automation layer, and initially connect AI-MALL through a 
curated catalog, vendor recommendations, and referrals.
Before production launch, conﬁrm the oﬃcial API, webhooks, authentication, pricing, data-
protection policy, and support details with the AI-MALL/UWO team. Without that 
conﬁrmation, the workﬂow should not claim to provide live agent purchases, real-time 
pricing, automatic vendor chat, or agent execution.
Recommended next actions
1.Send the oﬃcial integration questionnaire to AI-MALL/UWO.
2.Create an initial catalog of 10‒20 veriﬁed AI applications.
3.Prepare the WhatsApp welcome, qualiﬁcation, and human-handoﬀ ﬂows.
4.Test the webhook using a Meta test number or AISA Connect demo account.
5.Prepare approved templates and the consent process.
6.Validate the workﬂow with a limited pilot of 20‒50 users.
7.Decide on direct API integration based on pilot metrics and oﬃcial technical 
conﬁrmation.

Subject: [Action Required] Enable 2-step verification to maintain your access to the Google Cloud console

2SV will be required for Google Cloud console access starting Oct 20, 2026.




MY CONSOLE




Hello Tech,

We're writing to inform you about an upcoming security update for your  
organization.

Starting October 20, 2026, you will be required to use 2-Step Verification  
(2SV) to access the Google Cloud console.

We have provided additional information below to guide you through this  
change.

What you need to know

In November 2024, we first announced that Google Cloud would be doing a  
phased roll out of mandatory 2SV, also known as multi-factor authentication  
(MFA). Two-step verification adds an additional layer of security by  
requiring users to provide both a password and a second verification  
method—such as a security key, a phone-based prompt, or a Google  
Authenticator code—during sign in.

Key changes:

Starting October 20, 2026, you must use 2SV to access the Google Cloud  
console and Firebase console with your Google Cloud Identity account.

Your administrator can extend this deadline by 90 days. Watch for updates  
from your IT department about the final date when your organization will  
enforce 2SV.

What you need to do

Action advised: If you're using Google Cloud organization 1072058966898,  
you must turn on 2-Step Verification for your account at  
security.google.com by October 20, 2026.

If you cannot see the 2SV option, contact your administrator for assistance.

What is not affected:


Apps and workloads that run on Google Cloud, including those using Google  
APIs
Google Workspace products, such as Gmail, Google Sheets, and Google Slides.  
These have their own 2SV requirement programs. Review the 2SV requirements  
for the Google products you use.

We're here to help

We understand that this change may require some planning, and we're here to  
support you during this process. For more information, refer to the  
multi-factor authentication requirement documentation. If you have  
questions or need assistance, contact your administrator.

Thanks for choosing Google Cloud.





– The Google Cloud Team

 Hello, 


 We're writing to inform you about some updates to our Privacy Policy 
<https://anthropic.com/privacy>. 


 These changes only affect consumer accounts (Claude Free, Pro, and Max 
plans). If you use Claude Team, Claude Enterprise, the Claude Platform, or 
other services under our Commercial Terms or other agreements, then these 
changes don't apply to you.


What's changing? 


 Claude can do more than ever — taking on bigger tasks and connecting with the 
apps you use. We've updated our Privacy Policy to be clearer about the data we 
collect and how we use it. We encourage you to read the updated Privacy Policy 
in full, but we’ve set out a summary of the key changes below:


1. Multi-step tasks and connected apps. As Claude takes on more multi-step 
tasks and works with third-party apps and services, we've explained the data 
this involves — including how data can flow to and from third parties when you 
connect a service or have Claude do tasks on your behalf.


2. Verification data. As part of our measures to keep our services safe and 
secure we may ask you to verify your age or identity, and we've described what 
we collect and how.


3. Study participation. If you take part in Anthropic studies, surveys, or 
interviews, we've explained the information we collect.


4. Additional information about our data practices. We’ve provided more detail 
about how we communicate with you and promote our services, including providing 
tailored recommendations about our services that may be of interest to you. 
We've also clarified the circumstances under which we may receive or provide 
data to third parties, and the legal bases we rely on when processing your data.


 While our products have evolved, our commitments haven't: We don’t sell your 
data, Claude remains ad-free, and you can control whether your chats and coding 
sessions are used to train and improve Anthropic’s AI models.


Learn more 


 For detailed information about these changes: 


 *  Review the updated Privacy Policy <https://anthropic.com/privacy> 
 *  Visit our Privacy Center 
<https://privacy.claude.com/en/collections/10663362-consumers> for more

Hi Tech, we've refined how permissions work in Attio. Here's what's changed.  

Attio ( https://attio.com/?utm_campaign=%5B26+0430%5D+Permission+changes+-+everyone+else%2C+non-affected+workspaces&utm_content=%5B26+0430%5D+Permission+changes+-+everyone+else%2C+not+affected&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io )

Sign in ( https://app.attio.com/?utm_campaign=%5B26+0430%5D+Permission+changes+-+everyone+else%2C+non-affected+workspaces&utm_content=%5B26+0430%5D+Permission+changes+-+everyone+else%2C+not+affected&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io )

Hi Tech, we've refined how access works in Attio.

Permissions are returning to additive only, so the most permissive grant always wins, whether it's set at the workspace, team, or individual level.

Start with safe defaults at the workspace level, then grant more access to specific teams or people as needed. Each level can only grant more access, not less.

Nothing you've already set up needs to change. All your existing permissions will continue to work as expected.

This change was made to simplify permissions for workflows.

Workflows now inherit the workspace
default again, making them easier to build as members and agents increasingly work side by side.

You can read more in our Help Center ( https://attio.com/help/reference/productivity-collaborating/sharing-and-permissions?utm_campaign=%5B26+0430%5D+Permission+changes+-+everyone+else%2C+non-affected+workspaces&utm_content=%5B26+0430%5D+Permission+changes+-+everyone+else%2C+not+affected&utm_medium=email_action&utm_source=customer.io ), or reply to this email if you have questions.

मैंने recent outbound campaigns के email content, subject lines, actual attachments, recipient targeting और reply-pattern को product-wise audit किया है। Same template के hundreds of duplicate mails को अलग-अलग पढ़ने के बजाय प्रत्येक campaign का representative content + attachment + replies देखा है।

निष्कर्ष साफ है:

Problem products में कम है; outreach architecture में ज्यादा है।
Content देखने में professional है, लेकिन recipient-fit, subject, offer, attachment size, personalization और follow-up conversion कमजोर हैं।

Product-wise Audit

Campaign	Rating	मुख्य समस्या	क्या बदलना है
AI Legal → Law Colleges	5/10	Generic subject, बहुत लंबा mail, 2 भारी PDFs, बहुत सारे features	AI Legal-only pitch + specific academic outcome
AISA/AISA Connect → Schools	4/10	Wrong contacts + generic mail + deck mismatch	School-specific single use-case
EFV → Bookstores/Distributors	5.5/10	Philosophy ज्यादा, buyer economics कम	1-page trade sell sheet
Incubators/Funding	5.5/10	UWO ecosystem बहुत broad, ask भी 5 दिशाओं में	One primary thesis + traction + specific ask
EFV Pulse → Samsung	8/10 content	Execution error: Samsung spelling/address	Correct contact + tighter technical follow-up
AI Mall → Partners	6/10	Recipient से “plan choose” करवाया जा रहा है	Recommended pilot खुद propose करें
AI Legal → Marketing Agencies	7/10	CAC/budget/funnel data missing	Growth brief + exact commercial target

1. AI Legal colleges वाला campaign — सबसे बड़ा correction चाहिए

एक current law-college email का subject है:

“UWO™ | Building Applied AI & DeepTech Systems for the Real World”

जबकि recipient law college है और वास्तविक proposition AI Legal academic engagement है। Subject में न “AI Legal”, न “Law”, न student/faculty benefit है। UWO™ | Building Applied AI & DeepTech Systems for the Real World

Mail खुद काफी लंबा है—research, drafting, moot court, careers, challenges, internships, research, AISA, AISA Connect आदि सब एक ही first email में डाल दिए गए हैं। साथ में 19-page AI Legal deck ~7.25 MB + Education deck ~4.4 MB, यानी करीब 11.6 MB attachments जा रहे हैं। UWO™ | Building Applied AI & DeepTech Systems for the Real World

Recent period में इस generic law-college subject से लगभग 100 emails गए और meaningful inbound reply लगभग नहीं दिखा।

यह strong signal है कि template काम नहीं कर रहा।

क्या होना चाहिए: first email 100–130 words. One offer:

“30-minute AI Legal Faculty & Student Demo + 7-Day Institutional Evaluation”

और CTA:

“Would Tuesday 12 PM or Wednesday 3 PM work for a 15-minute faculty discussion?”

“Please let us know a convenient time” की जगह दो concrete slots दें।

⸻

2. Schools वाला AISA/AISA Connect campaign — यहाँ content से पहले targeting खराब है

Current email एक साथ AISA को student tutor और AISA Connect को institutional automation बेचता है। Empowering Your Students & Faculty with AI Institutional Ecosystem (UWO™)

इसमें सबसे गंभीर attachment issue मिला:

Education Deck के page 2 में target audience लिखा है: AI Companies, Startups, Enterprises, SMBs, Developers, Agencies आदि।

और mission AI tools discover/compare/adopt करने की बात करता है।

यह school deck में बिल्कुल नहीं होना चाहिए।

Principal deck खोले और दूसरे page पर startups/SMBs पढ़े तो credibility तुरंत गिरती है।

दूसरी बड़ी problem database है। कई mails:

* careers@
* recruitment@
* admissions@
* generic info@

पर जा रहे हैं।

एक school ने तो reply ऐसे किया जैसे UWO ने job application भेजी हो। इसका मतलब recipient selection गलत है।

Schools के लिए दो अलग campaigns बनाइए:

Campaign A — Principal/Management:
Admission Enquiry + Parent Communication + AI Helpdesk Automation.

Campaign B — Academic Head:
Responsible AI Literacy + Faculty Enablement + Student AI Programme.

दोनों को एक mail में न मिलाएँ।

⸻

3. EFV distribution — product अच्छा present है, लेकिन buyer को गलत चीज बेची जा रही है

Current EFV email में philosophy, author background, science-spirituality-AI, सभी editions, पूरा ISBN/MRP table और partnership benefits हैं। Distribution & Sales Partnership Opportunity – EFV Canon™ Book Series

लेकिन bookstore/distributor का पहला सवाल यह नहीं है कि EFV philosophy क्या है।

उनके सवाल हैं:

Margin कितना? Return policy? Stock ready? MOQ? Dispatch time? Category? Current sell-through? Marketing support? Sample copy?

Current 13-page, ~7.2 MB EFV deck में “mental health crisis”, human consciousness, technology/values आदि ज्यादा हैं। Trade buyer के लिए इसकी जरूरत कम है।

सबसे महत्वपूर्ण evidence:

एक simpler EFV outreach पर Motilal Banarsidass ने सीधे हर title की review copy मांगी।

इसका मतलब EFV में interest संभव है; process गलत है।

EFV के लिए केवल 1-page Trade Sell Sheet भेजनी चाहिए:

Book cover | Title | ISBN | MRP | Trade discount | Distributor margin | Available stock | Language | Pages | Category | Review copy | Contact.

और targets अलग करें:

Publisher ≠ Distributor ≠ Bookstore ≠ Library.

Jaico/Yoda जैसे publishers ने इसीलिए decline किया क्योंकि वे बाहरी titles distribute ही नहीं करते।

⸻

4. Incubation/Funding mails — बहुत broad हैं

Current generic incubation email एक साथ मांग रहा है:

Mentorship + Funding + Grants + R&D + Compute + Enterprise access + Investors.

और इसके साथ 18-page, ~14.4 MB company deck जा रहा है। Strategic Incubation & Collaboration Proposal | UWO™ – AI & Deep-Tech Ecosystem

Deck में भी AISA + AI Mall + AISA Connect + EFV सब बराबर intensity से आते हैं।

Incubator सोचता है:

“इनका primary business आखिर है क्या?”

और deck में कुछ claims aggressive हैं:

“fully de-risked”, “175 countries”, “up to 70%”, “months to minutes”, “100+ trademarks and 3 patents”.

जहाँ patent अभी filed/application stage में हो, वहाँ “3 patents” के बजाय “3 patent applications filed / patent-backed IP” कहना बेहतर है।

Dear Mr. Oluwatobi,

Thank you for such a detailed and well-researched assessment of the EFV Canon™ ecosystem.

We would be pleased to explore a formal collaboration with you to execute this strategy. Given your background and understanding of the opportunity, we would be particularly interested in exploring your role as a strategic market-development and distribution partner for the priority international markets.

To help us align the commercial and operational framework, could you please share your recommendations on the following:

1. Pilot Inventory Requirement
    For an initial market-entry pilot, what quantity of Volumes 1 and 2 would you recommend allocating for distribution, review copies, institutional outreach, and initial buyer testing?
2. Commercial & Engagement Model
    What structure would you propose for working together—for example, consulting/market-development fees, commission on sales, distribution margin, revenue share, or a hybrid model?
3. Initial Market Scope
    Would you recommend beginning with one priority country first, or simultaneously testing the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia on a controlled basis?
4. Pilot Deliverables
    For the first 30–60 days, what measurable deliverables would you propose in terms of distributor identification, buyer outreach, introductions, institutional opportunities, meetings, sample requests, and commercial discussions?

Once we receive your recommendations, we can finalize and share the international commercial sheet covering pricing, margins, MOQ, fulfilment, payment terms, stock availability, returns, and territory arrangements.

Our objective is to build a measurable path from:

Market Assessment → Qualified Buyers → Meetings → Samples/Reviews → Commercial Terms → Initial Orders

We look forward to your proposed structure and next steps.

Warm regards,

Ayush Dubey

Market Assessment → Qualified Buyers → Meetings → Samples/Reviews → Commercial Terms → Initial Orders

👋 Welcome to AI-Mall

Looking for an AI solution for your business?

मैंने recent outbound campaigns के email content, subject lines, actual attachments, recipient targeting और reply-pattern को product-wise audit किया है। Same template के hundreds of duplicate mails को अलग-अलग पढ़ने के बजाय प्रत्येक campaign का representative content + attachment + replies देखा है।

निष्कर्ष साफ है:

Problem products में कम है; outreach architecture में ज्यादा है।
Content देखने में professional है, लेकिन recipient-fit, subject, offer, attachment size, personalization और follow-up conversion कमजोर हैं।

Product-wise Audit

Campaign	Rating	मुख्य समस्या	क्या बदलना है
AI Legal → Law Colleges	5/10	Generic subject, बहुत लंबा mail, 2 भारी PDFs, बहुत सारे features	AI Legal-only pitch + specific academic outcome
AISA/AISA Connect → Schools	4/10	Wrong contacts + generic mail + deck mismatch	School-specific single use-case
EFV → Bookstores/Distributors	5.5/10	Philosophy ज्यादा, buyer economics कम	1-page trade sell sheet
Incubators/Funding	5.5/10	UWO ecosystem बहुत broad, ask भी 5 दिशाओं में	One primary thesis + traction + specific ask
EFV Pulse → Samsung	8/10 content	Execution error: Samsung spelling/address	Correct contact + tighter technical follow-up
AI Mall → Partners	6/10	Recipient से “plan choose” करवाया जा रहा है	Recommended pilot खुद propose करें
AI Legal → Marketing Agencies	7/10	CAC/budget/funnel data missing	Growth brief + exact commercial target

1. AI Legal colleges वाला campaign — सबसे बड़ा correction चाहिए

एक current law-college email का subject है:

“UWO™ | Building Applied AI & DeepTech Systems for the Real World”

जबकि recipient law college है और वास्तविक proposition AI Legal academic engagement है। Subject में न “AI Legal”, न “Law”, न student/faculty benefit है। UWO™ | Building Applied AI & DeepTech Systems for the Real World

Mail खुद काफी लंबा है—research, drafting, moot court, careers, challenges, internships, research, AISA, AISA Connect आदि सब एक ही first email में डाल दिए गए हैं। साथ में 19-page AI Legal deck ~7.25 MB + Education deck ~4.4 MB, यानी करीब 11.6 MB attachments जा रहे हैं। UWO™ | Building Applied AI & DeepTech Systems for the Real World

Recent period में इस generic law-college subject से लगभग 100 emails गए और meaningful inbound reply लगभग नहीं दिखा।

यह strong signal है कि template काम नहीं कर रहा।

क्या होना चाहिए: first email 100–130 words. One offer:

“30-minute AI Legal Faculty & Student Demo + 7-Day Institutional Evaluation”

और CTA:

“Would Tuesday 12 PM or Wednesday 3 PM work for a 15-minute faculty discussion?”

“Please let us know a convenient time” की जगह दो concrete slots दें।

⸻

2. Schools वाला AISA/AISA Connect campaign — यहाँ content से पहले targeting खराब है

Current email एक साथ AISA को student tutor और AISA Connect को institutional automation बेचता है। Empowering Your Students & Faculty with AI Institutional Ecosystem (UWO™)

इसमें सबसे गंभीर attachment issue मिला:

Education Deck के page 2 में target audience लिखा है: AI Companies, Startups, Enterprises, SMBs, Developers, Agencies आदि।

और mission AI tools discover/compare/adopt करने की बात करता है।

यह school deck में बिल्कुल नहीं होना चाहिए।

Principal deck खोले और दूसरे page पर startups/SMBs पढ़े तो credibility तुरंत गिरती है।

दूसरी बड़ी problem database है। कई mails:

* careers@
* recruitment@
* admissions@
* generic info@

पर जा रहे हैं।

एक school ने तो reply ऐसे किया जैसे UWO ने job application भेजी हो। इसका मतलब recipient selection गलत है।

Schools के लिए दो अलग campaigns बनाइए:

Campaign A — Principal/Management:
Admission Enquiry + Parent Communication + AI Helpdesk Automation.

Campaign B — Academic Head:
Responsible AI Literacy + Faculty Enablement + Student AI Programme.

दोनों को एक mail में न मिलाएँ।

⸻

3. EFV distribution — product अच्छा present है, लेकिन buyer को गलत चीज बेची जा रही है

Current EFV email में philosophy, author background, science-spirituality-AI, सभी editions, पूरा ISBN/MRP table और partnership benefits हैं। Distribution & Sales Partnership Opportunity – EFV Canon™ Book Series

लेकिन bookstore/distributor का पहला सवाल यह नहीं है कि EFV philosophy क्या है।

उनके सवाल हैं:

Margin कितना? Return policy? Stock ready? MOQ? Dispatch time? Category? Current sell-through? Marketing support? Sample copy?

Current 13-page, ~7.2 MB EFV deck में “mental health crisis”, human consciousness, technology/values आदि ज्यादा हैं। Trade buyer के लिए इसकी जरूरत कम है।

सबसे महत्वपूर्ण evidence:

एक simpler EFV outreach पर Motilal Banarsidass ने सीधे हर title की review copy मांगी।

इसका मतलब EFV में interest संभव है; process गलत है।

EFV के लिए केवल 1-page Trade Sell Sheet भेजनी चाहिए:

Book cover | Title | ISBN | MRP | Trade discount | Distributor margin | Available stock | Language | Pages | Category | Review copy | Contact.

और targets अलग करें:

Publisher ≠ Distributor ≠ Bookstore ≠ Library.

Jaico/Yoda जैसे publishers ने इसीलिए decline किया क्योंकि वे बाहरी titles distribute ही नहीं करते।

⸻

4. Incubation/Funding mails — बहुत broad हैं

Current generic incubation email एक साथ मांग रहा है:

Mentorship + Funding + Grants + R&D + Compute + Enterprise access + Investors.

और इसके साथ 18-page, ~14.4 MB company deck जा रहा है। Strategic Incubation & Collaboration Proposal | UWO™ – AI & Deep-Tech Ecosystem

Deck में भी AISA + AI Mall + AISA Connect + EFV सब बराबर intensity से आते हैं।

Incubator सोचता है:

“इनका primary business आखिर है क्या?”

और deck में कुछ claims aggressive हैं:

“fully de-risked”, “175 countries”, “up to 70%”, “months to minutes”, “100+ trademarks and 3 patents”.

जहाँ patent अभी filed/application stage में हो, वहाँ “3 patents” के बजाय “3 patent applications filed / patent-backed IP” कहना बेहतर है।

Incubator को चाहिए:

Problem → Product → Traction → Revenue → Customers → Team → Why this incubator → Exact ask.

Contrast देखिए: IIM Sirmaur वाला personalized outreach successful हुआ, formal application तक गया और अब 11 September pitch के लिए shortlisted है।

यानी incubation strategy dead नहीं है—generic blast की जगह institutional-specific approach काम कर रही है।

⸻

5. Samsung email — content अच्छा, लेकिन execution में serious गलती

EFV Pulse Samsung mail बाकी campaigns से काफी बेहतर है। इसमें:

data accuracy → technical alignment → validation → PoC → 90-day evaluation

की logical progression है। EFV Pulse™ x Samsung | Collaboration Deck & Technical Guidance

लेकिन recipient address गया:

S.ankush@sumsung.com

और attachment का नाम भी:

“EFV Pulse™ X Sumsung Deck.pdf” 

यह सबसे avoidable error है।

Deck technically अच्छा है, लेकिन एक page में AISA और EFV books को “Our Readiness Level – Live & Global” दिखाया गया है। Samsung को EFV Pulse की readiness जाननी है, दूसरे products की नहीं।

उस slide को replace करें:

Patent/IP → Current Prototype → Algorithms Ready → Tech Team → What exists today → What Samsung enables.

⸻

6. AI Mall / PerspectAI — warm lead को cold follow-up बना दिया

Meeting हो चुकी है। इसके बाद repeatedly यह पूछा गया:

Which affiliate plan would you like to proceed with?

इससे decision-making का पूरा काम partner पर डाल दिया गया।

Warm partnership में UWO को recommendation देनी चाहिए:

“We recommend a 30-day launch pilot: ₹0 onboarding, X% revenue share, listing live within 48 hours, joint review after 30 days.”

फिर पूछें:

“Can we proceed with this structure?”

यह yes/no decision है। Reply probability बहुत ज्यादा होती है compared with “आप कौन सा plan चुनेंगे?”

⸻

7. AI Legal marketing agencies

Digidarts वाला post-meeting email professional है। Product deck, pricing, App Store links सभी दिए हैं। AI Legal™ Marketing & Launch | Unified Web Options (UWO™)

लेकिन agency के लिए critical inputs missing हैं:

Current installs
Registrations
Paid users
Monthly revenue
Current CAC
Monthly ad budget
Target CAC
Primary persona
Trial-to-paid conversion
30-day target

इसके बिना agency generic “strategy proposal” ही देगी।

और pricing PDF बहुत dense है—multiple workspaces, plans, credits और dozens of limits।

Marketing agency को 5-page pricing encyclopedia नहीं चाहिए।

उन्हें चाहिए:

Hero Offer → ₹X → Target Persona → Trial → Conversion event → LTV → Maximum CAC

⸻

असली कमी कहाँ है?

मेरे audit के अनुसार approximate diagnosis:

Product / basic content: 7/10
Visual decks: 7/10
Product-recipient fit: 5/10
Email subject/first 5 seconds: 4/10
Database/decision-maker accuracy: 3/10
Offer clarity: 4/10
CTA: 4/10
Follow-up system: 5/10
Commercial proof: 4/10

यानी emails खराब लिखे हुए नहीं हैं—वे sales conversion के लिए बने हुए नहीं हैं।

सबसे बड़ी गलती है:

हम recipient को UWO के बारे में बहुत कुछ बता रहे हैं, लेकिन recipient को reply करने का पर्याप्त कारण नहीं दे रहे।

अब क्या करना चाहिए

1. Generic bulk email sending फिलहाल reduce करें। Hundreds of identical mails भेजने की जगह प्रत्येक team member रोज 20–30 verified decision-makers पर targeted outreach करे।
2. First cold email में heavy deck मत भेजें। Maximum एक 1-page PDF under ~500 KB. Full deck reply/meeting के बाद या link से दें।
3. हर product के लिए अलग Sales Kit बने: one buyer, one problem, one offer, one CTA. UWO ecosystem first mail में न बेचें।
4. Recipient verification compulsory करें: Name, designation, department, email, LinkedIn/phone. Generic careers/recruitment addresses हटाएँ।
5. Follow-up multichannel करें: Day 0 email → Day 2 LinkedIn/phone → Day 4 short value follow-up → Day 7 final specific proposal. एक ही “just following up” copy बार-बार न भेजें।
6. Existing warm leads पहले close करें: Samsung correct contact, Motilal sample dispatch, IIM Sirmaur pitch, PerspectAI commercial pilot, Growth Hackers paid pilot discussion. ये cold email से ज्यादा valuable हैं।
7. Team की daily report अब Emails Sent नहीं होनी चाहिए। उसे बनाइए:

Verified Leads → Delivered → Replies → Qualified Replies → Meetings → Proposals → Paid Closures

मेरी recommendation है कि अब UWO के लिए 6 final conversion-ready master systems बनें: AI Legal Colleges, Schools/AISA Connect, EFV Distribution, Incubation/Funding, AI Mall Partnerships, UWO Connect B2B—हर एक में final email + subject + 1-page attachment structure + follow-up sequence हो। यही current response problem को सबसे तेजी से correct करेगा।

 
Update all today

AI Legal → Law Colleges	5/10	Generic subject, बहुत लंबा mail, 2 भारी PDFs, बहुत सारे features	AI Legal-only pitch + specific academic outcome
AISA/AISA Connect → Schools	4/10	Wrong contacts + generic mail + deck mismatch	School-specific single use-case
EFV → Bookstores/Distributors	5.5/10	Philosophy ज्यादा, buyer economics कम	1-page trade sell sheet
Incubators/Funding	5.5/10	UWO ecosystem बहुत broad, ask भी 5 दिशाओं में	One primary thesis + traction + specific ask
EFV Pulse → Samsung	8/10 content	Execution error: Samsung spelling/address	Correct contact + tighter technical follow-up
AI Mall → Partners	6/10	Recipient से “plan choose” करवाया जा रहा है	Recommended pilot खुद propose करें
AI Legal → Marketing Agencies	7/10	CAC/budget/funnel data missing	Growth brief + exact commercial target

1. AI Legal colleges वाला campaign — सबसे बड़ा correction चाहिए

एक current law-college email का subject है:

“UWO™ | Building Applied AI & DeepTech Systems for the Real World”

जबकि recipient law college है और वास्तविक proposition AI Legal academic engagement है। Subject में न “AI Legal”, न “Law”, न student/faculty benefit है। UWO™ | Building Applied AI & DeepTech Systems for the Real World

Mail खुद काफी लंबा है—research, drafting, moot court, careers, challenges, internships, research, AISA, AISA Connect आदि सब एक ही first email में डाल दिए गए हैं। साथ में 19-page AI Legal deck ~7.25 MB + Education deck ~4.4 MB, यानी करीब 11.6 MB attachments जा रहे हैं। UWO™ | Building Applied AI & DeepTech Systems for the Real World

Recent period में इस generic law-college subject से लगभग 100 emails गए और meaningful inbound reply लगभग नहीं दिखा।

यह strong signal है कि template काम नहीं कर रहा।

क्या होना चाहिए: first email 100–130 words. One offer:

“30-minute AI Legal Faculty & Student Demo + 7-Day Institutional Evaluation”

और CTA:

“Would Tuesday 12 PM or Wednesday 3 PM work for a 15-minute faculty discussion?”

“Please let us know a convenient time” की जगह दो concrete slots दें।

⸻

2. Schools वाला AISA/AISA Connect campaign — यहाँ content से पहले targeting खराब है

Current email एक साथ AISA को student tutor और AISA Connect को institutional automation बेचता है। Empowering Your Students & Faculty with AI Institutional Ecosystem (UWO™)

इसमें सबसे गंभीर attachment issue मिला:

Education Deck के page 2 में target audience लिखा है: AI Companies, Startups, Enterprises, SMBs, Developers, Agencies आदि।

और mission AI tools discover/compare/adopt करने की बात करता है।

यह school deck में बिल्कुल नहीं होना चाहिए।

Principal deck खोले और दूसरे page पर startups/SMBs पढ़े तो credibility तुरंत गिरती है।

दूसरी बड़ी problem database है। कई mails:

* careers@
* recruitment@
* admissions@
* generic info@

पर जा रहे हैं।

एक school ने तो reply ऐसे किया जैसे UWO ने job application भेजी हो। इसका मतलब recipient selection गलत है।

Schools के लिए दो अलग campaigns बनाइए:

Campaign A — Principal/Management:
Admission Enquiry + Parent Communication + AI Helpdesk Automation.

Campaign B — Academic Head:
Responsible AI Literacy + Faculty Enablement + Student AI Programme.

दोनों को एक mail में न मिलाएँ।

⸻

3. EFV distribution — product अच्छा present है, लेकिन buyer को गलत चीज बेची जा रही है

Current EFV email में philosophy, author background, science-spirituality-AI, सभी editions, पूरा ISBN/MRP table और partnership benefits हैं। Distribution & Sales Partnership Opportunity – EFV Canon™ Book Series

लेकिन bookstore/distributor का पहला सवाल यह नहीं है कि EFV philosophy क्या है।

उनके सवाल हैं:

Margin कितना? Return policy? Stock ready? MOQ? Dispatch time? Category? Current sell-through? Marketing support? Sample copy?

Current 13-page, ~7.2 MB EFV deck में “mental health crisis”, human consciousness, technology/values आदि ज्यादा हैं। Trade buyer के लिए इसकी जरूरत कम है।

सबसे महत्वपूर्ण evidence:

एक simpler EFV outreach पर Motilal Banarsidass ने सीधे हर title की review copy मांगी।

इसका मतलब EFV में interest संभव है; process गलत है।

EFV के लिए केवल 1-page Trade Sell Sheet भेजनी चाहिए:

Book cover | Title | ISBN | MRP | Trade discount | Distributor margin | Available stock | Language | Pages | Category | Review copy | Contact.

और targets अलग करें:

Publisher ≠ Distributor ≠ Bookstore ≠ Library.

Jaico/Yoda जैसे publishers ने इसीलिए decline किया क्योंकि वे बाहरी titles distribute ही नहीं करते।

⸻

4. Incubation/Funding mails — बहुत broad हैं

Current generic incubation email एक साथ मांग रहा है:

Mentorship + Funding + Grants + R&D + Compute + Enterprise access + Investors.

और इसके साथ 18-page, ~14.4 MB company deck जा रहा है। Strategic Incubation & Collaboration Proposal | UWO™ – AI & Deep-Tech Ecosystem

Deck में भी AISA + AI Mall + AISA Connect + EFV सब बराबर intensity से आते हैं।

Incubator सोचता है:

“इनका primary business आखिर है क्या?”

और deck में कुछ claims aggressive हैं:

“fully de-risked”, “175 countries”, “up to 70%”, “months to minutes”, “100+ trademarks and 3 patents”.

जहाँ patent अभी filed/application stage में हो, वहाँ “3 patents” के बजाय “3 patent applications filed / patent-backed IP” कहना बेहतर है।

Incubator को चाहिए:

Problem → Product → Traction → Revenue → Customers → Team → Why this incubator → Exact ask.

Contrast देखिए: IIM Sirmaur वाला personalized outreach successful हुआ, formal application तक गया और अब 11 September pitch के लिए shortlisted है।

यानी incubation strategy dead नहीं है—generic blast की जगह institutional-specific approach काम कर रही है।

⸻

5. Samsung email — content अच्छा, लेकिन execution में serious गलती

EFV Pulse Samsung mail बाकी campaigns से काफी बेहतर है। इसमें:

data accuracy → technical alignment → validation → PoC → 90-day evaluation

की logical progression है। EFV Pulse™ x Samsung | Collaboration Deck & Technical Guidance

लेकिन recipient address गया:

S.ankush@sumsung.com

और attachment का नाम भी:

“EFV Pulse™ X Sumsung Deck.pdf” 

यह सबसे avoidable error है।

Deck technically अच्छा है, लेकिन एक page में AISA और EFV books को “Our Readiness Level – Live & Global” दिखाया गया है। Samsung को EFV Pulse की readiness जाननी है, दूसरे products की नहीं।

उस slide को replace करें:

Patent/IP → Current Prototype → Algorithms Ready → Tech Team → What exists today → What Samsung enables.

⸻

6. AI Mall / PerspectAI — warm lead को cold follow-up बना दिया

Meeting हो चुकी है। इसके बाद repeatedly यह पूछा गया:

Which affiliate plan would you like to proceed with?

इससे decision-making का पूरा काम partner पर डाल दिया गया।

Warm partnership में UWO को recommendation देनी चाहिए:

“We recommend a 30-day launch pilot: ₹0 onboarding, X% revenue share, listing live within 48 hours, joint review after 30 days.”

फिर पूछें:

“Can we proceed with this structure?”

यह yes/no decision है। Reply probability बहुत ज्यादा होती है compared with “आप कौन सा plan चुनेंगे?”

⸻

7. AI Legal marketing agencies

Digidarts वाला post-meeting email professional है। Product deck, pricing, App Store links सभी दिए हैं। AI Legal™ Marketing & Launch | Unified Web Options (UWO™)

लेकिन agency के लिए critical inputs missing हैं:

Current installs
Registrations
Paid users
Monthly revenue
Current CAC
Monthly ad budget
Target CAC
Primary persona
Trial-to-paid conversion
30-day target

इसके बिना agency generic “strategy proposal” ही देगी।

और pricing PDF बहुत dense है—multiple workspaces, plans, credits और dozens of limits।

Marketing agency को 5-page pricing encyclopedia नहीं चाहिए।

उन्हें चाहिए:

Hero Offer → ₹X → Target Persona → Trial → Conversion event → LTV → Maximum CAC

⸻

असली कमी कहाँ है?

मेरे audit के अनुसार approximate diagnosis:

Product / basic content: 7/10
Visual decks: 7/10
Product-recipient fit: 5/10
Email subject/first 5 seconds: 4/10
Database/decision-maker accuracy: 3/10
Offer clarity: 4/10
CTA: 4/10
Follow-up system: 5/10
Commercial proof: 4/10

यानी emails खराब लिखे हुए नहीं हैं—वे sales conversion के लिए बने हुए नहीं हैं।

सबसे बड़ी गलती है:

हम recipient को UWO के बारे में बहुत कुछ बता रहे हैं, लेकिन recipient को reply करने का पर्याप्त कारण नहीं दे रहे।

अब क्या करना चाहिए

1. Generic bulk email sending फिलहाल reduce करें। Hundreds of identical mails भेजने की जगह प्रत्येक team member रोज 20–30 verified decision-makers पर targeted outreach करे।
2. First cold email में heavy deck मत भेजें। Maximum एक 1-page PDF under ~500 KB. Full deck reply/meeting के बाद या link से दें।
3. हर product के लिए अलग Sales Kit बने: one buyer, one problem, one offer, one CTA. UWO ecosystem first mail में न बेचें।
4. Recipient verification compulsory करें: Name, designation, department, email, LinkedIn/phone. Generic careers/recruitment addresses हटाएँ।
5. Follow-up multichannel करें: Day 0 email → Day 2 LinkedIn/phone → Day 4 short value follow-up → Day 7 final specific proposal. एक ही “just following up” copy बार-बार न भेजें।
6. Existing warm leads पहले close करें: Samsung correct contact, Motilal sample dispatch, IIM Sirmaur pitch, PerspectAI commercial pilot, Growth Hackers paid pilot discussion. ये cold email से ज्यादा valuable हैं।
7. Team की daily report अब Emails Sent नहीं होनी चाहिए। उसे बनाइए:

Verified Leads → Delivered → Replies → Qualified Replies → Meetings → Proposals → Paid Closures

मेरी recommendation है कि अब UWO के लिए 6 final conversion-ready master systems बनें: AI Legal Colleges, Schools/AISA Connect, EFV Distribution, Incubation/Funding, AI Mall Partnerships, UWO Connect B2B—हर एक में final email + subject + 1-page attachment structure + follow-up sequence हो। यही current response problem को सबसे तेजी से correct करेगा।

 
Update all today

payload.title:
⚖️ “Is the case ready?”

That message from a senior can come at any time.

But being ready means more than simply having a case file.

You need to:

📌 Summarize the facts
📌 Identify the key issues
📌 Structure the relevant law
📌 Organize important information
📌 Prepare working notes
📌 Build the foundation for drafting and arguments

When information is scattered across files and notes, preparation can quickly become time-consuming.

AI Legal™ helps bring scattered legal information into a more organized workflow-so you can prepare case facts, issues, relevant law and working notes in one place.

The goal isn't to wait for the senior's message.

The goal is to be prepared before it arrives. ⚖️🤖

🚀 Make your legal workflow smarter with AI Legal™.

📲 AI Legal™ is now LIVE on Google Play Store and Apple App Store.

[Google Play Store](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.uwo.ailegal&utm_source=chatgpt.com)
[Apple App Store](https://apps.apple.com/in/app/ai-legal/id6797449251?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Don't Just Read. Understand the Law.

#AILegal #LegalAI #LegalTech #CasePreparation #LegalResearch #ArtificialIntelligence
